title: OpenAI keys without long-lived secrets: workload identity federation or automated rotation, before the 2026-12-01 key expiry
description:
Ryan, 2026-11-01: the new OpenAI API key lasts 30 days (expires about 2026-12-01). Implement OpenAI's federated (workload identity) access with automated key rotation well before then.

Where the key lives today (papyrus-production 712236451410), all SecureString:
- /papyrus/shipped/openai-api-key (Shipped knowledge run, KNOWLEDGE_OPENAI_KEY_PARAMETER)
- /papyrus/p-apyr-us/openai-api-key
- /papyrus/search/openai-api-key (search provider layer, #963)
- /amplify/shared/<appId>/OPENAI_API_KEY for threat-intelligence-cms d12wnrx15qbcc2, distinctive-cms d2xke8ygmrzqpp, dataparade-cms d35q7zv4zad2we (Amplify secret() resolved at Lambda cold start)
- ~/Projects/Papyrus/.env for local runs

Previous key was revoked without warning on 2026-11-01; the Shipped knowledge run failed at ai-review with HTTP 401.

Plan:
1. Research what OpenAI offers today for federated workload identity (OIDC from AWS IAM roles, short-lived tokens) and its admin API for project keys and rotation. Write up the options.
2. Preferred: callers obtain short-lived OpenAI credentials from their AWS role (no stored key). Fallback: one SSM parameter per site plus a scheduled rotation Lambda that mints a new project key via the admin API, writes SSM, verifies it, then revokes the old one.
3. Collapse the copies to one parameter per site, read through one helper in papyrus_content.
4. Alarm on 401 from OpenAI anywhere (knowledge run, editorial checks, search) and on rotation failure, notifying the site alarm topic.
5. Docs plus Gherkin for rotation and the 401 alarm.

Acceptance: no OpenAI key needs manual replacement; a rotation runs end to end in production before 2026-12-01.
